## alleleTableToSeekDeepProcessClusters {#alleleTableToSeekDeepProcessClusters}

Turn an allele table from another pipeline (one row per sample, target and haplotype with its read count, e.g. MAD4HatTeR's allele data) into the directory layout processClusters reads, popClustering/\<target\>/\<sample\>/\<sample\>/output.fasta.gz with each haplotype's read count in its name

```bash
SeekDeep alleleTableToSeekDeepProcessClusters --help
```

**Required Options**

*Miscellaneous*

| Flag | Description | Default | Type |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--alleleTableFnp` | results tab delimited file, each row is a haplotype, should have at least 4 columns,  sample (--sampleColName),within sample read count (--withinSampleReadCntColName), haplotype sequence (--hapSeqColName), target name column (--targetNameColName) **(required)** |  | boost::filesystem::path |

**Optional Options**

*Output Directory*

| Flag | Description | Default | Type |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--dout` | Output Directory Name | `./` | std::string |
| `--overWriteDir` | If the directory already exists over write it | `false` | bool |

*Results Column Names*

| Flag | Description | Default | Type |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--hapSeqColName` | Haplotype Sequence Column Name | `asv` | std::string |
| `--sampleColName` | sample Column Name | `sampleID` | std::string |
| `--targetNameColName` | target Name Column Name, the column name in the table which indicates the different targets | `locus` | std::string |
| `--withinSampleReadCntColName` | within Sample Read Cnt Col Column Name | `reads` | std::string |

*Miscellaneous*

| Flag | Description | Default | Type |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--debug` | Debug | `false` | bool |
| `--excludeSamples` | Exclude these select samples from analysis | `None` | std::set\<std::string\> |
| `--excludeTargets` | Exclude these select targets from analysis | `None` | std::set\<std::string\> |
| `--outputFnp` | name of the fasta file written in each sample's directory | `output.fasta.gz` | boost::filesystem::path |
| `--selectSamples` | Only analyze these select samples | `None` | std::set\<std::string\> |
| `--selectTargets` | Only analyze these select targets | `None` | std::set\<std::string\> |
| `--targetKeyFnp` | target Key  Fnp, tab delimited assumed first column old name and second column new name, unless columns provided with targetKeyOldTargetNameColName and targetKeyNewTargetNameColName arguments |  | boost::filesystem::path |
| `--targetKeyNewTargetNameColName` | if renaming targets, target Key New Target Name Col Name |  | std::string |
| `--targetKeyOldTargetNameColName` | if renaming targets, target Key Old Target Name Col Name |  | std::string |
| `--verbose`<br>`-v` | Verbose | `false` | bool |

## ampliconReadQC {#ampliconReadQC}

Report what the read pairs of targeted amplicon samples are, on their expected target or primer dimers and other off target products, directly from the reads without extraction or clustering

```bash
SeekDeep ampliconReadQC --help
```

**Required Options**

*Input*

| Flag | Description | Default | Type |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--primers` | A file with the columns target,forward primer,reverse primer **(required)** |  | boost::filesystem::path |

**Optional Options**

*Genomes*

| Flag | Description | Default | Type |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--errors` | Number of errors to allow in primers when finding them in the genomes, only used when creating --targetInfoDir | `2` | uint32_t |
| `--genomeDir` | A directory of the target genomes, named GENOME.fasta, to create --targetInfoDir if it's not given and to BLAST products that aren't what was expected against |  | boost::filesystem::path |
| `--gffDir` | A directory with a gff for the genomes in --genomeDir, only used when creating --targetInfoDir |  | boost::filesystem::path |
| `--hostGenome` | A fasta of the host genome to BLAST products that aren't what was expected against |  | boost::filesystem::path |
| `--pairedEndLength` | The length of the reads, only used when creating --targetInfoDir, by default it's taken from the reads | `0` | uint32_t |
| `--primaryGenome` | The primary reference genome in --genomeDir |  | std::string |
| `--selectedGenomes` | Other genomes in --genomeDir to use, separated by commas, leave blank to use all of them |  | std::string |

*Input*

| Flag | Description | Default | Type |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--fastqDir` | A directory of samples, first mates end in _R1_001, _R1 or _1 and the second mates are the same with a 2, what comes before that is the sample name |  | boost::filesystem::path |
| `--overlapStatusFnp` | A file with the columns target,status for how each target is expected to overlap, instead of --targetInfoDir |  | boost::filesystem::path |
| `--sampleName` | Name of the sample when giving just one with the fastq options |  | std::string |
| `--sampleTable` | A tab delimited table of samples with the columns sample,r1,r2 |  | boost::filesystem::path |
| `--targetInfoDir` | The output directory of SeekDeep genTargetInfoFromGenomes, for how each target is expected to overlap, its reference sequences, and where it is, if this isn't given it gets created from --genomeDir |  | boost::filesystem::path |

*Output Directory*

| Flag | Description | Default | Type |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--dout` | Output Directory Name | `./` | std::string |
| `--overWriteDir` | If the directory already exists over write it | `false` | bool |

*Placing Products*

| Flag | Description | Default | Type |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--adapterKmerLen` | How many bases in a row have to match an adapter | `8` | uint32_t |
| `--adapters` | A fasta of the adapter sequences to check products for instead of the TruSeq ones, a hit to adapter says nothing about where a sequence came from since many database records have some left in them |  | boost::filesystem::path |
| `--blastDust` | The low complexity masking for BLASTing longer sequences, the blast default of "20 64 1" hides too much of an AT rich genome and turning it off with "no" is orders of magnitude slower | `40 64 1` | std::string |
| `--blastMinCoverage` | The lowest fraction of the sequence a BLAST hit has to cover to count | `0.85` | double |
| `--blastMinPercentId` | The lowest percent identity for a BLAST hit to count | `95` | double |
| `--maxSeqsToBlast` | Only the most common sequences across all the samples are BLASTed if there's more than this, the rest are reported as notBlasted | `20000` | uint32_t |
| `--minBlastLen` | Sequences shorter than this are too short to place with any confidence | `25` | uint32_t |
| `--targetRegionFlank` | How far from a target a BLAST hit can be and still count as being in that target | `100` | uint32_t |

*Primer Dimers*

| Flag | Description | Default | Type |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--maxGapBetweenPrimers` | The most bases allowed between the primers at each end of a read for it to be a dimer, the primers can also overlap or abut | `20` | uint32_t |
| `--minCandidateMatchBases` | The fewest bases of a primer that have to match at a read's end for it to be kept as a possible partner of a trusted primer at the other end, which makes the read an unresolved dimer | `5` | uint32_t |
| `--minPrimerMatchBases` | The fewest bases of a primer that have to match at a read's end for it to be trusted, 0 to work it out from the number of primers since the more primers there are the more likely a short match is by chance | `0` | uint32_t |

*Primers*

| Flag | Description | Default | Type |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--checkRevComplementForPrimers` | Also check whether the mates are the other way around when the forward primer isn't found on the first mate | `false` | bool |
| `--primerCallCacheMaxEntries` | Max number of distinct read starts per sample to remember the primer found for so it's not searched for again, 0 to not remember any, the output is the same either way | `200000` | uint32_t |
| `--primerNumOfMismatches` | The number of mismatches to allow in primers | `3` | uint32_t |
| `--primerSearchStart` | By default the primers are searched at the very beginning of seq, use this flag to start the search here | `0` | uint32_t |
| `--primerWithinStart` | By default the primers are searched at the very beginning of seq, use this flag to extended the search, should be kept low to cut down on false positives | `0` | uint32_t |
| `--useAlnPrimerSearch` | Use alignment to search for primers rather than motif search, motif search is faster but alignment search allows indels | `false` | bool |

*Reading Sequence Input*

| Flag | Description | Default | Type |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--fastq1` | Input sequence filename, only need 1, fastq first mate text file |  | boost::filesystem::path |
| `--fastq1gz` | Input sequence filename, only need 1, fastq first mate gzipped file |  | boost::filesystem::path |
| `--fastq2` | Input sequence filename, only needed with --fastq1, fastq second mate text file |  | boost::filesystem::path |
| `--fastq2gz` | Input sequence filename, only needed with --fastq1gz, fastq second mate gzipped file |  | boost::filesystem::path |
| `--lower` | How to handle Lower Case Bases | `nothing` | std::string |
| `--processed` | Processed, Input Sequence Name has a suffix that contains abundance info | `false` | bool |
| `--removeGaps` | Remove Gaps from Input Sequences | `false` | bool |
| `--trimAtWhiteSpace` | Remove everything after first whitespace character in input sequence name | `false` | bool |

*Reference Kmer Comparison*

| Flag | Description | Default | Type |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--compKmerLen` | The size of the kmers for comparing to the reference sequences | `5` | uint32_t |
| `--compKmerSimCutOff` | The fraction of kmers that have to be shared with a reference sequence | `0.5` | double |
| `--noKmerComparison` | Don't compare reads to the reference sequences of their target | `false` | bool |
| `--refSeqsDir` | A directory of TARGET.fasta reference sequences to compare reads to, by default the ones in --targetInfoDir |  | boost::filesystem::path |

*Stitching*

| Flag | Description | Default | Type |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--dimerOverLapErrorAllowed` | The same as --overLapErrorAllowed but for a second attempt at stitching the pairs that failed, only used to find primer dimers | `0.05` | double |
| `--hardMismatchCutOff` | A hard cut off for number of mismatches in the overlap when stitching | `20` | uint32_t |
| `--hqMismatchCutOff` | A hard cut off for number of high quality mismatches in the overlap when stitching | `10` | uint32_t |
| `--lqMismatchCutOff` | A hard cut off for number of low quality mismatches in the overlap when stitching | `10` | uint32_t |
| `--minOverlap` | The minimal amount of overlap when stitching | `8` | uint32_t |
| `--noTrimLowQualWindows` | Don't Trim Low Qual Windows | `false` | bool |
| `--overLapErrorAllowed` | The fraction of high quality mismatches to allow in the overlap when stitching, rounds down so an overlap under 1/this bases is allowed none, should be the same as what the extraction will use | `0.02` | double |
| `--qWindowSize` | Quality Window Trim Size | `5` | uint32_t |
| `--qWindowStep` | Quality Window Trim Step | `1` | uint32_t |
| `--qWindowTrimAvgQualCutOff` | Quality Window Trim Avg Qual Cut Off | `25` | double |
| `--r1Trim` | Remove this many bases off of the end of r1 reads | `1` | uint32_t |
| `--r2Trim` | Remove this many bases off of the end of r2 reads | `1` | uint32_t |
| `--stitchCacheMaxEntries` | Max number of mate pairs per sample to remember the alignment of so that they only have to be aligned once, 0 to not remember any, the output is the same either way | `500000` | uint32_t |
| `--stitchMatchScore` | The score for a match when aligning the mates to stitch them | `2` | int32_t |
| `--stitchMismatchPenalty` | The penalty for a mismatch when aligning the mates to stitch them, harsher than the match score so a long low identity placement of the mates doesn't out score a short true overlap | `4` | uint32_t |

*Miscellaneous*

| Flag | Description | Default | Type |

| `--debug` | Debug | `false` | bool |
| `--numThreads` | Number of samples to process at the same time and threads for BLAST, the output is the same no matter the number of threads | `1` | uint32_t |
| `--verbose`<br>`-v` | Verbose | `false` | bool |

## assignTargetGenomes {#assignTargetGenomes}

Assign each target to the first of the given genomes SeekDeep genTargetInfoFromGenomes found it in, writes targetGenomes.tsv and a \<genome\>_variantCall.bed per genome with the inner regions of its targets (and their -R1/-R2 mates) for --genomicLocations, targets in none of the genomes aren't assigned

```bash
SeekDeep assignTargetGenomes --help
```

**Required Options**

*Miscellaneous*

| Flag | Description | Default | Type |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--genomes` | The genomes to assign targets to, in order, a target goes to the first it's in **(required)** | `None` | std::vector\<std::string\> |
| `--locations` | The locationsByGenome directory of SeekDeep genTargetInfoFromGenomes **(required)** |  | boost::filesystem::path |

**Optional Options**

*Miscellaneous*

| Flag | Description | Default | Type |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--dout` | Output directory | `assignedTargetGenomes` | boost::filesystem::path |
| `--overWriteDir` | Overwrite the output directory | `false` | bool |
| `--verbose`<br>`-v` | Verbose | `false` | bool |

## benchmarkControlMixturesOnProcessedClustersDir {#benchmarkControlMixturesOnProcessedClustersDir}

Benchmark one target's processClusters output directory against known control mixtures, classifying each control sample's haplotypes as expected or false by comparing them to the expected strain sequences, writes classifiedHaplotypes.tsv, performancePerTarget.tsv and the false haplotypes compared to the expected and to the other haplotypes

Also callable as `benchmarkControlMixtures`.

```bash
SeekDeep benchmarkControlMixturesOnProcessedClustersDir --help
```

**Required Options**

*Miscellaneous*

| Flag | Description | Default | Type |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--expectedSeqsFnp` | Expected Seqs fasta file **(required)** |  | boost::filesystem::path |
| `--mixtureSetUp` | Mixture Set Up, 3 columns 1)MixName, 2)strain, 3)relative_abundance **(required)** |  | boost::filesystem::path |
| `--name` | Name to give the current analysis **(required)** |  | std::string |
| `--processClustersDir` | Process Clusters Dir **(required)** |  | boost::filesystem::path |
| `--sampleToMixture` | Sample To Mixture, 2 columns 1)sample, 2)MixName **(required)** |  | boost::filesystem::path |

**Optional Options**

*Alignment*

| Flag | Description | Default | Type |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--caseInsensitive` | Use Case Insensitive Scoring for alignment | `false` | bool |
| `--countEndGaps` | Count End Gaps | `false` | bool |
| `--degen` | Use Degenerative Base Scoring for alignment | `false` | bool |
| `--gap` | Gap Penalties for Middle Gap | `5,1` | std::string |
| `--gapAll` | Gap Penalties for All (middle and end gaps) | `5,1` | std::string |
| `--gapLeft` | Gap Penalties for Left End Gap | `5,1` | std::string |
| `--gapRight` | Gap Penalties for Right End Gap | `0,0` | std::string |
| `--lessN` | Use Degenerative Base Scoring but use a lesser score for the degenerative bases | `false` | bool |
| `--local` | Local alignment | `false` | bool |
| `--match` | Match score for alignment | `2` | int32_t |
| `--mismatch` | Mismatch score for alignment | `-2` | int32_t |
| `--noHomopolymerIndelWeighting` | Don't do Homopolymer Weighting | `false` | bool |
| `--scoreMatrix` | Score Matrix Filename |  | std::string |
| `--use_blosum62` | Use blosum62 scoring | `false` | bool |

*Caching Alignments*

| Flag | Description | Default | Type |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--alnInfoDir` | Alignment Info Cache Directory Name |  | std::string |
| `--outAlnInfoDir` | Alignment Info Cache Out Directory Name |  | std::string |

*Low Frequency Mismatch Determination*

| Flag | Description | Default | Type |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--expandKmerPos` | Expand Kmer Position Found At | `false` | bool |
| `--expandKmerSize` | Expand Kmer Size for extending where kmers where found | `5` | uint32_t |
| `--kAnywhere` | Count Kmers without regard for position | `false` | bool |
| `--kLength` | Kmer Length | `9` | uint32_t |
| `--runCutOff` | Kmer frequency cut off for a mismatch to be considered low frequency | `.45%,10` | std::string |

*Mismatch Quality Determination*

| Flag | Description | Default | Type |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--qualThres` | Quality Thresholds, should go PrimaryQual,SecondaryQual | `20,15` | std::string |
| `--qualThresWindow` | Quality Threshold Window Length | `2` | uint32_t |

*Output Directory*

| Flag | Description | Default | Type |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--dout` | Output Directory Name | `./` | std::string |
| `--overWriteDir` | If the directory already exists over write it | `false` | bool |

*Miscellaneous*

| Flag | Description | Default | Type |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--debug` | Debug | `false` | bool |
| `--fillInMissingSamples` | Fill in missing Samples with placeholders | `false` | bool |
| `--hqMismatches` | Allowable high quality mismatches | `0` | uint32_t |
| `--largeBaseIndel` | Allowable large base indels (\>2 bases) | `0` | double |
| `--lqMismatches` | Allowable low quality mismatches | `0` | uint32_t |
| `--metaFnp` | meta data for the control samples |  | boost::filesystem::path |
| `--newColumnElement` | What to Add to the Table Under new Column, can be comma delimited when adding multiple new columns |  | std::string |
| `--newColumnName` | Name of a new Column to add to table, can be comma delimited to add multiple |  | std::string |
| `--oneBaseIndel` | Allowable one base indels | `0` | double |
| `--popSeqsFnp` | Population Sequences, can be the expected controls but also as any sequence done |  | boost::filesystem::path |
| `--scoreBased` | Scored Based Comparison For Alignments(defualt:event based) | `false` | bool |
| `--skipMissingSamples` | Skip Samples if they are missing | `false` | bool |
| `--twoBaseIndel` | Allowable two base indels | `0` | double |
| `--verbose`<br>`-v` | Verbose | `false` | bool |

## benchmarkTarAmpControlMixtures {#benchmarkTarAmpControlMixtures}

Benchmark one target's results table (one row per sample haplotype, e.g. processClusters selectedClustersInfo) against known control mixtures, the single target version of benchmarkMultiTarAmpControlMixtures, writes the same classified haplotype and performance tables

```bash
SeekDeep benchmarkTarAmpControlMixtures --help
```

**Required Options**

*Miscellaneous*

| Flag | Description | Default | Type |
|---|---|---|---|

## mixturesToExpectedPmo {#mixturesToExpectedPmo}

Make an expected PMO of what each control sample should have for benchmarkMultiTarAmpControlMixtures --expectedPmoFnp. Library samples are the control samples and their specimen is their mixture, a specimen name has characters the PMO doesn't allow replaced by _ and keeps the mixture name in a mix_name field. Each strain's allele is a representative microhaplotype named by the allele with the strain as an extra field. A sample's reads are pseudo counts that add up to about --pseudoCountTotal, each allele's share is its strain's relative abundance times its copies from --strainAllelesFnp (1 if not listed). Identical alleles are kept separate here, the benchmark combines them within each sample.

```bash
SeekDeep mixturesToExpectedPmo --help
```

**Required Options**

*Miscellaneous*

| Flag | Description | Default | Type |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--expectedSeqsDirFnp` | Expected Seqs directory of fasta files, one per target named \<target\>.fasta or \<target\>.fasta.gz, sequences named by strain or by allele from --strainAllelesFnp **(required)** |  | boost::filesystem::path |
| `--mixtureSetUp` | Mixture Set Up, 3 columns 1)MixName, 2)strain, 3)relative_abundance **(required)** |  | boost::filesystem::path |
| `--sampleToMixture` | Sample To Mixture, 2 columns 1)sample, 2)MixName, can have a target column (--targetNameColName) along with --mixtureSetUp to have different samples and mixtures per target **(required)** |  | boost::filesystem::path |

**Optional Options**

*Writing Output*

| Flag | Description | Default | Type |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--appendFile` | Append to file | `false` | bool |
| `--out` | Out Filename | `expectedControls` | boost::filesystem::path |
| `--overWrite` | Over Write Existing Files | `false` | bool |

*Miscellaneous*

| Flag | Description | Default | Type |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--debug` | Debug | `false` | bool |
| `--excludeTargets` | exclude these targets | `None` | std::set\<std::string\> |
| `--panelName` | panel name | `expected_controls` | std::string |
| `--primers` | Optional, SeekDeep id file with the targets' primers, targets without primers get NA primers and the fake_primers attribute |  | boost::filesystem::path |
| `--pseudoCountTotal` | the pseudo counts for a sample's target add up to about this, the benchmark turns them back into frequencies | `1000000` | uint32_t |
| `--selectTargets` | only these targets | `None` | std::set\<std::string\> |
| `--strainAllelesFnp` | Optional, for strains with more than one copy or allele at a target (e.g. a copy number variant), tab delimited with columns target, strain, allele and optionally copies (copies of that allele per genome, default 1), the alleles are named in the --expectedSeqsDirFnp fasta, each allele's share of the template is its strain's relative abundance times its copies, strains not listed have one copy named after the strain |  | boost::filesystem::path |
| `--targetNameColName` | the target column in the mixture tables if they're split by target | `p_name` | std::string |
| `--trimBack` | trim this many bases from the back of every expected seq, e.g. to match a pipeline that trims the edges of the insert | `0` | uint32_t |
| `--trimFront` | trim this many bases from the front of every expected seq, e.g. to match a pipeline that trims the edges of the insert | `0` | uint32_t |
| `--verbose`<br>`-v` | Verbose | `false` | bool |

## nanoporeAmpliconReadQC {#nanoporeAmpliconReadQC}

Report what the nanopore reads of targeted amplicon samples are, complete amplicons, joined amplicons, folds, and off target products, directly from the reads without extraction or clustering. Reads should have adapters and barcodes trimmed

```bash
SeekDeep nanoporeAmpliconReadQC --help
```

**Required Options**

*Input*

| Flag | Description | Default | Type |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--primers` | A file with the columns target,forward primer,reverse primer **(required)** |  | boost::filesystem::path |

**Optional Options**

*Barcodes*

| Flag | Description | Default | Type |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--barcodeKey` | A file with the columns barcode,sample, the number in the barcode's name is the barcode's number |  | boost::filesystem::path |
| `--barcodeLen` | The length of the barcode in the sequences in --barcodes | `0` | uint32_t |
| `--barcodeStart` | Where the barcode starts in the sequences in --barcodes, they can have flanking sequence | `0` | uint32_t |
| `--barcodes` | A fasta of the sample barcodes to look for at the junctions of joined amplicons, another sample's barcode there means the amplicons can't be said to belong to this sample |  | boost::filesystem::path |

*Complete Amplicons*

| Flag | Description | Default | Type |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--decoyEvery` | Also search for shuffled primers on 1 in this many reads to see how often the search finds something by chance, 0 to skip | `20` | uint32_t |
| `--lenToleranceFrac` | How far off the expected length a complete amplicon can be as a fraction of it, whichever of this and --minLenTolerance is larger | `0.25` | double |
| `--maxPrimerError` | The fraction of a primer that can be edits, reads with joined amplicons are also counted at 0.15 and 0.10 to see how much depends on this | `0.2` | double |
| `--minInnerKmerFrac` | The fraction of kmers between the primers that have to be in the target's reference sequences | `0.3` | double |
| `--minLenTolerance` | How far off the expected length a complete amplicon can be, at least | `40` | uint32_t |
| `--otherBasesCutOff` | The most bases outside a read's only complete amplicon before it's ampliconPlusOther | `100` | uint32_t |

*Folds*

| Flag | Description | Default | Type |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--kmerLen` | The size of the kmers that vote for a fold | `13` | uint32_t |
| `--minAnchors` | The fewest kmers that have to pair between the arms | `5` | uint32_t |
| `--minAnchorsPerBase` | The fewest kmers that have to pair per base of the anchored part of the arm | `0.03` | double |
| `--minArmLen` | The shorter arm of a fold has to be at least this long | `60` | uint32_t |
| `--minIdentity` | The lowest identity between the arms | `0.7` | double |
| `--primerAtStartWithin` | A read's first primer has to start within this many bases to place its fold on the amplicon | `60` | uint32_t |
| `--turnBinSize` | The bin size for where folds turn along an amplicon | `20` | uint32_t |

*Input*

| Flag | Description | Default | Type |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--fastqDir` | A directory of samples, a file for each, the file's name is the sample's name |  | boost::filesystem::path |
| `--includeUndetermined` | Include files in --fastqDir that start with Undetermined, by default they're skipped since they aren't a sample, only --maxCappedReads of their reads are looked at | `false` | bool |
| `--maxCappedReads` | At most about this many reads of inputs that aren't a sample, chosen by a hash of the read's name so the same reads are chosen every time | `500000` | uint64_t |
| `--mismatchedSamplesFastq` | The file of reads the demultiplexing found with different samples at each end, only --maxCappedReads of them are looked at |  | boost::filesystem::path |
| `--refSeqsDir` | A directory of TARGET.fasta reference sequences without their primers, instead of --targetInfoDir |  | boost::filesystem::path |
| `--sampleName` | Name of the sample when giving just one, by default the name of the input file |  | std::string |
| `--targetInfoDir` | The output directory of SeekDeep genTargetInfoFromGenomes, for the targets' reference sequences |  | boost::filesystem::path |

*Other Categories*

| Flag | Description | Default | Type |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--maxDimerInsert` | The most bases between two primers on a read for it to be a dimer | `30` | uint32_t |
| `--minTargetKmerFrac` | The fraction of a read or fold arm's kmers that have to be a target's to say it's that target | `0.3` | double |
| `--otherTargetKmerFrac` | The fraction of a read's kmers that have to be a second target's to say it holds both | `0.1` | double |

*Output*

| Flag | Description | Default | Type |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--noFoldbackReads` | Don't write foldbackReads.tsv.gz, every read with a fold, can be most of a sample | `false` | bool |
| `--noSalvageReads` | Don't write salvageReads.tsv.gz, where the complete amplicons are on the reads with 2 or more | `false` | bool |
| `--writeReadCategories` | Write readCategories.tsv.gz, a line for every read | `false` | bool |

*Output Directory*

| Flag | Description | Default | Type |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--dout` | Output Directory Name | `./` | std::string |
| `--overWriteDir` | If the directory already exists over write it | `false` | bool |

*Placing Reads*

| Flag | Description | Default | Type |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--mappingIndex` | A minimap2 index of the target genome and the host, to say where reads and folds are, reads are only placed if this is given |  | boost::filesystem::path |

| `--offTargetLocusBinSize` | The bin size for where twoPrimerOffTarget reads map to, by the start of the read's longest alignment | `1000` | uint32_t |
| `--targetBed` | Where the panel is on the target genome, the columns chrom,start,end,name with the primers in the coordinates |  | boost::filesystem::path |

*Reading Sequence Input*

| Flag | Description | Default | Type |
|---|---|---|---|

## setupTarAmpAnalysis {#setupTarAmpAnalysis}

Set up a full targeted amplicon analysis from a directory of raw read files and a primers file, works out the sample names and writes the extractor, qluster (or kluster), processClusters and popClusteringViewer commands for every sample and target into --outDir, with runAnalysis.sh to run them all

```bash
SeekDeep setupTarAmpAnalysis --help
```

**Required Options**

| Flag | Description | Default | Type |

R1BeginsInR2=target size \< read length (causes read through), R1EndsInR2=target size \> read length but less than 2 x read length, NoOverlap=target size \> 2 x read length and can't be combined with the others **(required)** |  | boost::filesystem::path |

*Input*

| Flag | Description | Default | Type |

|---|---|---|---|

| `--extraExtractorCmds` | Extra extractor cmds to add to the defaults |  | std::string |
| `--extraProcessClusterCmds` | Extra process clusters cmds to add to the defaults |  | std::string |
| `--extraProcessClusterCmdsPerTarget` | Extra process clusters cmds to add to the defaults, table needs cols, 1)target,2)extraProcessClusterCmds |  | boost::filesystem::path |
| `--extraQlusterCmds`<br>`--extraKlusterCmds` | Extra qluster/kluster cmds to add to the defaults |  | std::string |
| `--extraQlusterCmdsPerTarget`<br>`--extraKlusterCmdsPerTarget` | Extra qluster/kluster cmds to add to the defaults per target, table needs cols, 1)target,2)extraQlusterCmds |  | boost::filesystem::path |
| `--numberOfFilesToInvestigate` | Number of files to investigate when adding additional recommended flags | `10` | uint32_t |
| `--primerWithinToInvesitgate` | primer within distant to investigate when adding additional recommended flags | `40` | uint32_t |
| `--testNumberOfReadsToInvestigate` | Number of reads per file to investigate when adding additional recommended flags | `10000` | uint32_t |

## testForFoldbacks {#testForFoldbacks}

Find reads that are a foldback (inverse chimera), a stretch of sequence and then its reverse complement, and where on the read the fold is, using only the read so it works on reads from anywhere and doesn't need a reference or target. Reads should have their adapters and barcodes trimmed, the same adapter on both ends of a molecule reads as a short inverted repeat and gets called

```bash
SeekDeep testForFoldbacks --help
```

**Required Options**

*Reading Sequence Input*

| Flag | Description | Default | Type |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--fasta` | Input sequence filename, only need 1, fasta text file **(required)** |  | boost::filesystem::path |
| `--fastagz` | Input sequence filename, only need 1, fasta gzipped file **(required)** |  | boost::filesystem::path |
| `--fastq` | Input sequence filename, only need 1, fastq text file **(required)** |  | boost::filesystem::path |
| `--fastqgz` | Input sequence filename, only need 1, fastq gzipped file **(required)** |  | boost::filesystem::path |

**Optional Options**

*Detection*

| Flag | Description | Default | Type |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--extensionBand` | How far apart the arms can get from insertions and deletions when finding the arms' ends | `16` | uint32_t |
| `--extensionXDrop` | Stop extending an arm when the score has fallen this far below its best | `12` | int32_t |
| `--kmerLen` | The size of the kmers that vote for a fold | `13` | uint32_t |
| `--maxChainGap` | The furthest apart two paired kmers can be and still be on the same arms | `150` | uint32_t |
| `--maxKmerOccurrences` | Kmers seen more than this many times in a read don't vote | `4` | uint32_t |
| `--maxLoopFlank` | See --maxLoopPerArm | `100` | uint32_t |
| `--maxLoopPerArm` | The loop between the arms can be at most this times the longer arm plus --maxLoopFlank | `3` | double |
| `--minAnchors` | The fewest kmers that have to pair between the arms | `5` | uint32_t |
| `--minAnchorsPerBase` | The fewest kmers that have to pair per base of the anchored part of the arm | `0.03` | double |
| `--minArmLen` | The shorter arm of a fold has to be at least this long | `60` | uint32_t |
| `--minIdentity` | The lowest identity between the arms | `0.7` | double |
| `--seedBand` | The width of the range of kmer position sums that the strongest fold is looked for within | `30` | uint32_t |

*Output Directory*

| Flag | Description | Default | Type |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--dout` | Output Directory Name | `./` | std::string |
| `--overWriteDir` | If the directory already exists over write it | `false` | bool |

*Reading Sequence Input*

| Flag | Description | Default | Type |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--lower` | How to handle Lower Case Bases | `nothing` | std::string |
| `--processed` | Processed, Input Sequence Name has a suffix that contains abundance info | `false` | bool |
| `--removeGaps` | Remove Gaps from Input Sequences | `false` | bool |
| `--trimAtWhiteSpace` | Remove everything after first whitespace character in input sequence name | `false` | bool |

*Miscellaneous*

| Flag | Description | Default | Type |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--debug` | Debug | `false` | bool |
| `--numThreads` | Number of threads, the output is the same no matter the number of threads | `1` | uint32_t |
| `--sampleName` | Name of the sample for the output, by default the name of the input file |  | std::string |
| `--verbose`<br>`-v` | Verbose | `false` | bool |
| `--writeAllCandidates` | Write every read with any reverse complement kmers in it, with the column called saying which passed, for trying out other cut offs | `false` | bool |

## variantCallOnSeqAndProtein {#variantCallOnSeqAndProtein}

Call nucleotide and amino acid variants on the haplotypes in a results table (e.g. processClusters selectedClustersInfo) by aligning each target's haplotypes to the genome and translating them over the genes they cover, writes each target's calls plus combined genomic and protein VCFs and amino acid change tables to reports/ in the output directory

```bash
SeekDeep variantCallOnSeqAndProtein --help
```

**Required Options**

*Translation Output*

| Flag | Description | Default | Type |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--genomeFnp`<br>`--genome` | Genome file so final haplotypes can be mapped to a genome **(required)** |  | boost::filesystem::path |
| `--gffFnp`<br>`--gff` | Gff file to intersect the final haplotypes with genes to get translations **(required)** |  | boost::filesystem::path |

*Miscellaneous*

| Flag | Description | Default | Type |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--resultsFnp` | results tab delimited file, each row is a haplotype, should have at least 4 columns, 1) sample (--sampleColName), 2)within sample read count (--withinSampleReadCntColName), 3)haplotype pop ID (--popHapIdColName), 4)target name column (--targetNameColName), and a 5th col with the hap sequence (--popHapSeqColName) unless read in from --popSeqsDirFnp **(required)** |  | boost::filesystem::path |

**Optional Options**

*Output Directory*

| Flag | Description | Default | Type |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--dout` | Output Directory Name | `./` | std::string |
| `--overWriteDir` | If the directory already exists over write it | `false` | bool |

*PMO*

| Flag | Description | Default | Type |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--pmo` | A PMO with the haplotypes in --resultsFnp, the variant calls are added to its haplotypes by sequence and it's written to reports/allPMO.json.gz |  | boost::filesystem::path |
| `--pmoGenomeName` | Name of the genome variants were called against for the PMO, defaults to the genome file name without its extension |  | std::string |
| `--pmoGenomeTaxonIds` | NCBI taxonomy ids of the genome for the PMO, e.g. 36329 | `None` | std::vector\<unsigned int\> |
| `--pmoGenomeUrl` | Where the genome can be downloaded, for the PMO | `NA` | std::string |
| `--pmoGenomeVersion` | Version of the genome for the PMO, defaults to the genome name |  | std::string |
| `--pmoGffUrl` | Where the genome's annotation can be downloaded, for the PMO |  | std::string |

*Results Column Names*

| Flag | Description | Default | Type |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--popHapIdColName` | popHapIdColName | `h_popUID` | std::string |
| `--popHapSeqColName` | population Haplotype Sequence Column Name, the seq to call variants on | `h_Consensus` | std::string |
| `--sampleColName` | sample Column Name | `s_Sample` | std::string |
| `--targetNameColName` | target Name Column Name, the column name in the table which indicates the different targets | `p_name` | std::string |
| `--withinSampleReadCntColName` | within Sample Read Cnt Col Column Name | `c_ReadCnt` | std::string |

*Translation Output*

| Flag | Description | Default | Type |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--aaExpand` | Amount to expand the protein for when aligning | `10` | uint32_t |
| `--allowableStopCodons` | The number of stop codons to allow in a translation, if contains more than than the translation will be filtered off | `1` | uint32_t |
| `--correct_small_homopolymer_errors` | correct small homopolymer errors based on alignment to reference within cDNA | `false` | bool |
| `--doNotWriteOutGeneInfos` | Do Not Write Out Gene Infos that intersect with seqs | `false` | bool |
| `--knownAminoAcidChangesFnp` | Known Amino Acid Changes, must have at least 2 columns, positions are 1-postion-based (first position is 1), 1)TranscriptID, 2)AAPosition |  | boost::filesystem::path |
| `--max_hp_run_gap_size` | the maximum(inclusive) homopolymer error size to correct | `3` | uint32_t |
| `--min_hp_run_size_to_correct` | the homopolymer run in which to correct errors must be this size or great (inclusive) | `8` | uint32_t |
| `--useFullProtein` | Just use the full protein for aligning, could be more time consuming | `false` | bool |
| `--useLastz` | Use lastz for alignment | `false` | bool |

*Miscellaneous*

| Flag | Description | Default | Type |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--aaSummaryRefInfoNextToAlt` | In AA Summary table place the Reference Info Next To Alternate info, rather than stacked | `false` | bool |
| `--combineOverlappingCallsAcrossTargets` | Rather than taking the best variant call for overlapping targets, sum them instead | `false` | bool |
| `--complexVariantFractionOfCoveredSamples` | complex Variant Fraction Of Covered Samples | `0.95` | double |
| `--complexVariantFractionOfSamplesCoveringSpan` | Fraction of samples that must cover a complex variant's full span for it to be reported | `0.5` | double |
| `--complexVariantWithinDist` | The distance within to link complex variants | `15` | uint32_t |
| `--debug` | Debug | `false` | bool |
| `--doNotRequireFullKnownCoverage` | do Not Require Full Known Coverage e.g. will report covered by target if there is partial coverage | `false` | bool |
| `--doNotRescueVariantCallsAcrossTargets` | do Not Rescue Variant Calls Across Targets | `false` | bool |
| `--excludeSamples` | exclude these select samples from analyze | `None` | std::set\<std::string\> |
| `--excludeTargets` | exclude these select targets from analyze | `None` | std::set\<std::string\> |
| `--exportLabIsolateSeqs` | Export Lab Isolate Seqs, will export seqs with meta of site==LabIsolate | `false` | bool |
| `--genomicLocations` | a bed file with specific genomic locations to align to, location name needs to match target name |  | boost::filesystem::path |
| `--genomicLocationsChangePeriodToDash` | when supplying a location name, change periods to dashes in the name | `false` | bool |
| `--getPairwiseComps` | get Pairwise comparison metrics | `false` | bool |
| `--ignoreSubFields` | Meta Sub Field values to ignore when calculating variants, e.g. --ignoreSubFields "isFieldSample:TRUE,PreferredSample:FALSE" | `site:LabContaminated,site:LabControl,site:LabCross` | std::set\<std::string\> |
| `--mappingNumThreads` | Number of threads to use for the alignment portion | `1` | uint32_t |
| `--metaFieldsToCalcPopDiffs` | meta Fields To Calc Pop Diffs | `None` | std::vector\<std::string\> |
| `--metaFnp` | meta data for the samples |  | boost::filesystem::path |
| `--noDiagAlnPairwiseComps` | Use diagonal Alignment for Pairwise Comparisons | `false` | bool |
| `--numThreads` | Number of threads to use | `1` | uint32_t |
| `--perTargetVariantCallsDir` | Make the reports from variant calls already made per target instead of calling them, a target's calls (what collapseAndCallVariants writes) are in \<this\>/\<target\>/\<--perTargetVariantCallsSubDir\>, e.g. the variantCalling directories of processClusters and PathWeaver runProcessClustersOnRecon |  | boost::filesystem::path |
| `--perTargetVariantCallsSubDir` | The directory within each target's directory of --perTargetVariantCallsDir with its variant calls, e.g. variantCalling for PathWeaver runProcessClustersOnRecon output |  | std::string |
| `--ploidy` | Ploidy to force for the sample for the vcf files | `2` | uint32_t |
| `--popSeqsDirFnp` | Population Sequences, in this directory should be a fasta file with the name of each target |  | boost::filesystem::path |
| `--popSeqsRegexPatRemoval` | optional regex pattern to process the input pop sequences from --popSeqsDirFnp to make it match up with the input results folder | `_([tf])?\d+(\.\d+)?$` | std::string |
| `--selectSamples` | Only analyze these select samples | `None` | std::set\<std::string\> |
| `--selectTargets` | Only analyze these select targets | `None` | std::set\<std::string\> |
| `--skipMissingInputBedRegions` | when supplying a location skip warning on missing Input Bed Regions | `false` | bool |
| `--variantFrequencyCutOff` | Low Variant Cut Off, don't report variants below this frequency | `0.005` | double |
| `--variantOccurrenceCutOff` | Occurrence Cut Off, don't report variants below this count | `2` | uint32_t |
| `--variantTotalReadDepthCutOff` | Low Variant Total Read Depth Cut Off, don't report variants that have a summed total read depth less than this across all samples | `10` | uint32_t |
| `--verbose`<br>`-v` | Verbose | `false` | bool |
